operators.name: Ultimate Dog Sledding Experience
operators.summary: Ultimate Dog Sledding Experience runs guided winter sled tours on 250 acres of private woodland in Canton, Maine, with a short kennel visit before the trail and a yurt stop afterward. Guests can ride with a musher, or spend a full day learning to drive from a double-driver sled with the guide beside them.
operators.priceNote: All listed rates are per sled, not per person. The 1.5-hour tour is $400 on weekdays and $450 on weekends, holidays, and vacation weeks. The 2.5-hour tour is $600 and $650 on the same split. The full-day intro is $1,400 per sled on weekdays. The tours index also shows Grafton Notch at $1,500 per sled, and the homepage shows the Twilight trip at $950 per sled.
operators.priceQuote: All pricing is PER SLED, NOT per person!
operators.kidNote: The 1.5-hour tour is listed for ages 1 and older. Other tours list minimum ages of 2, 5, or 12. A sled may hold two adults, one adult and two children 8 or younger, or two adults and one toddler.

operators.name: Muddy Paw Sled Dog Kennel
operators.summary: Muddy Paw Sled Dog Kennel in Jefferson, New Hampshire, books hands-on winter sled tours and snowless cart rides for a kennel of nearly 90 dogs, including rescues. Guests meet the team before the trail, and a Musher for a Minute clinic puts them on a double-driver sled with a musher.
operators.season: Winter sleds mid-December through March; 2026 cart tours listed October 1 through December 7; kennel visits April through September
operators.priceNote: Winter sled rates are per sled, not per person. The 1.5-hour tour is $500 to $650 per sled depending on weekday, weekend, or holiday and on standard versus extended sled. The 3-hour tour is $750 per sled. Musher for a Minute is $675, $700, or $775 per sled. Separate per-person products: K9s & Kisses is $30, the 2-mile cart is $85 weekdays and $105 weekends, and the 5-mile cart is $135 weekdays and $155 weekends and holidays.
operators.priceQuote: $500 per standard sled (2 guests or 350lbs maximum)
operators.weightLimit: 350 lb on a standard winter sled; 425 lb on an extended winter sled
operators.kidNote: The site calls the trips family-friendly and open to ages 2 and up on most tours. Children under 2 cannot enter the kennel. The 3-hour tour and Musher for a Minute clinic are ages 12 and up.

operators.name: Eden Dogsledding
operators.summary: Eden Dogsledding in Eden, Vermont, runs reservation-only tours with the Un-Chained Gang on a private trail system within reach of Stowe, Smugglers Notch, and Jay Peak. Winter trips use snow sleds and the June-into-November season uses wheeled sleds, with harnessing and time with the dogs included.
operators.season: Snow tours described as December through April; dogsledding-on-wheels listed June into November 2026
operators.priceNote: Winter prices are per sled dog team with a guide, not per person. The winter page's 2026 block lists Alpha at $2,500, Beta at $1,750 plus tax, and Omega at $1,500 plus tax, with a $1,350 midweek rate for 1–2 people. The wheels page, headed open June into November 2026, lists Beta at $1,750, Omega at $1,500, and Alpha at $2,000 per tour, and the same page also shows older lower figures. An interaction kennel tour is listed at $100 per person with a $500 minimum.
operators.priceQuote: Every tour Price is per sled Dogteam with a professional guide (not per person)
operators.weightLimit: 350 lb combined on winter sleds (300 lb in March); 325 lb on summer carts
operators.kidNote: The site calls the tours family-friendly and describes an Omega option for small families with young children. The wheels page says children under 5 are welcome with supervision.

2026 winter per-sled rates, 350 lb limit, phone reservations only

operators.name: October Siberians Sled Dog Adventures
operators.summary: October Siberians runs dogsled tours at Little River State Park in Waterbury, Vermont, near Stowe and the Mad River Valley, and also lists a Smugglers Notch backup plus fall cart runs from its Hinesburg kennel. The sled is set up so one guest can drive while the musher keeps control and another guest rides in the bag.
operators.season: Winter weekends at Little River, with extra holiday days; fall cart training when it is cool enough
operators.duration: 2 hours at Little River, about 90 minutes on the sled
operators.priceNote: Little River rates are not a single per-person price. A 2-hour tour starts at $597 for two passengers, including the park fee, 6% sales tax, and booking and card fees. Added adults 13 and older are $298.50 and children 3 to 12 are $152; children under 3 are free. The large-group campground loop starts at $597 for four passengers. The adventures overview still shows an older 'starts at $545 for two' line.
operators.priceQuote: The 2 hours tours price starts at $597 for two passengers; this rate includes Park entrance fee, 6% sales tax, booking and CC fees.
operators.weightLimit: About 400 lb total for all passengers per sled
operators.kidNote: The site says the Siberians are great with children. Children under 12 must ride with an adult, and children under 3 are free on the Little River rates.

operators.name: Umiak Outdoor Outfitters
operators.summary: Umiak Outdoor Outfitters in Stowe, Vermont, sells a one-hour sled-dog meet-and-greet and a short evening dog-sled ride at Stoweflake Mountain Resort. Huskies in the Kingdom provides the evening ride, and Umiak is the site that lists the price and takes the booking.
operators.season: Evening rides offered seasonally on winter Saturdays
operators.duration: 30-minute evening program with about 15 minutes of riding; 1-hour meet-and-greet
operators.priceNote: Evening rides are $198 to $338 per sled, up to 3 people and 350 lb, not per person. The separate meet-and-greet is $29 to $39 per person and does not include a ride.
operators.weightLimit: 350 lb combined and 3 people per sled
operators.kidNote: Minimum age is 2 and minors must have an adult present. The meet-and-greet page calls the program a fit for families.

operators.name: Hilltown Sleddogs
operators.summary: Hilltown Sleddogs in West Chesterfield, Massachusetts, is a touring and racing kennel that lists dryland rig rides, dog-yard visits, and snow sled rides when there is enough snow. The snow ride includes harnessing and a lesson in driving the sled, and the site says winter ride slots are limited with fuller operations hoped for in 2027.
operators.season: Rides and lessons in winter, spring, and fall on dryland or snow; a November 27, 2026 vacation day camp is posted
operators.duration: 1.5-hour snow ride; 2-hour dryland training or rig ride
operators.priceNote: Snow sled rides and the 2-hour training or rig rides are $225 for one person and $375 for two, not a flat per-person rate. Added people after the pair are priced by age, from $50 to $150 on the snow ride. The site says winter ride numbers are limited.
operators.priceQuote: This 1.5-hour Sled Dog Adventure is $225 for 1 person and $375 for 2 people
operators.weightLimit: Under 230 lb per person on the snow sled ride; 225 lb per person on the training run
operators.kidNote: Snow-ride add-on prices start at ages 2 to 6. The site also sells kids sled-dog camps and dog-yard hikes.

sources.what: West Chesterfield kennel and November 27, 2026 camp notice
Current snow and dryland prices, driving lesson, per-person weight limits, limited winter rides

operators.name: Adirondack Kennel
operators.summary: Adirondack Kennel, now on New York's Tug Hill after years in the southern Adirondacks, posted a 2026 note that it is still taking a limited number of sled rides while racing. Rides meet in the town of Boylston at Winona Forest, and guests who want to can drive with the musher on a safety line.
operators.priceNote: Individual rides are $400 per sled for roughly 40 minutes, with four people maximum, not per person. A 10-minute kids loop is also $400 and requires at least 10 people; fewer than 10 still pay $400. A 3-hour winterfest block is $2,750.
operators.priceQuote: INDIVIDUAL RIDES: $400 Roughly 40 Minutes Four people max per sled.
operators.kidNote: The pricing page offers a short kids loop for no more than 30 kids and says the same $400 applies if fewer than 10 people book.

operators.name: Oregon Trail of Dreams
operators.summary: Oregon Trail of Dreams sells winter dog-sled rides that meet in the Lower Sunrise lot at Mt. Bachelor, where an eight-dog team runs a five-mile forest trail, plus a longer Cascade Lakes marathon trip. The hour ride is a guided introduction for ages 3 and up, and a separate race program is offered for people who want to learn to drive a team.
operators.season: Winter. One-hour tours Thursday through Monday. Marathon trips Thursday and Friday, with listed blackouts from December 22, 2025 through January 5, 2026 and on other 2026 holiday weekends.
operators.duration: 1 hour on the Mt. Bachelor tour; about 4 hours for the marathon
operators.priceNote: Hour-tour prices are per person. Sunday through Friday is $225 for an adult and $110 for a child 80 lb and under. Saturday is $235 and $115. Holiday rates are $240 and $125. The half-day marathon is $1,230 per trip, not per person, plus a $2 booking fee. The race-driving program says to call for fees.
operators.weightLimit: 450 lb and no more than 3 people per sled on the one-hour tour
operators.kidNote: The hour tour is described as suitable for ages 3 to 103. Children ages 3 to 12 must ride with an adult.

sources.what: Current Mt. Bachelor per-person prices, 450 lb limit, ages, and 2026 marathon blackouts
